**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 65, Verse 1 (Part 1 of 2)**

(p-139) Surat al-Talaq, also called al-Nisa' al-Qusra (the Lesser Women). Its central purpose is to establish the sound management of separation and departure, through refining character with taqwa (God-consciousness), especially in spending, especially when there is discord, especially when it concerns women, and especially at divorce, so that the separation takes the form of continued kindness and meeting. Its name is al-Talaq because it is the most comprehensive of the surahs on this subject. Likewise it is called al-Nisa' al-Qusra, because justice in separation is part of absolute justice, which is the focus of the aim of Surat al-Nisa'.

﴿In the name of Allah﴾, who possesses all the attributes of perfection. ﴿the Most Merciful﴾, whose bounty encompasses all by His mercy. ﴿the Most Compassionate﴾, who specially favours with mercy those of lofty aspiration.

* *

When al-Taghabun (Surah 64) was concluded by stating that He, may He be exalted, is Most Appreciative, Most Forbearing, Mighty and Wise, along with complete knowledge and all-encompassing power, and after the warning about wives being enemies, and since enmity leads to separation, He opened this surah by restraining souls when their desires surge, with the reins of taqwa. He addressed the foremost of creation with the utmost honour, directing the address to the highest of morals, to draw attention to the greatness of the rulings in this surah. These rulings are built upon the four names [of Allah], so that they are received with utmost eagerness. So He said: ﴿O Prophet﴾, specifying him (ﷺ), mentioning the attribute that is the cause of receiving the wondrous sciences and desired wisdoms and understandings.

When He knew from the Prophet's (ﷺ) readiness the greatness of the wisdom, and from (p-140) the use of the vocative with the particle of intermediacy, which is not used for a matter of great importance, that the one closest to the presence [of Allah], namely the Prophet (ﷺ), is not in every respect the one intended by it, and that the purpose is to draw attention to the majesty of these rulings and to exert effort in making them understood and acted upon, He therefore turned to the community once they became alert and listened attentively. He said, using the particle of certainty, since it is among its greatest uses: ﴿When you divorce﴾. It is known from this that the ruling is general, including him (ﷺ). However, since a person has two states with his wives, one of which is contention, the address in that case is more fitting for others. The second is generosity and reconciliation, through forbearance and pardon, and in this case he (ﷺ) is more fitting. Therefore, the Surah of al-Tahrim came to him (ﷺ).

﴿women﴾, meaning, if you intend to divorce this category of women, one or more of them. ﴿then divorce them﴾, meaning, if the husband wishes to divorce them, whether with three divorces or fewer. The fewer the better, as evidenced by what follows in the context regarding the reference to reconciliation. ﴿for their waiting period﴾, meaning, at a time, or at the start of the waiting period, that is, at the start of a purity period (tuhr) which is counted from it. This is the purity in which she has not been intercourse with, if she has been consummated. This is the meaning of the reading of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, "fi qubuli 'iddatihinna" (at the beginning of their waiting period). This is the talaq al-sunnah (the divorce in accordance with the Sunna), and other than it is talaq al-bid'ah (the innovated divorce), because divorce during menstruation prolongs the waiting period, as that period is not counted. It is necessary that the purity be one in which intercourse has not occurred, because if she has had intercourse, she may conceive, and the waiting period would be prolonged. This lam (for) denotes time, similar to in the phrase "write this for five days remaining in the month of such-and-such." It was chosen to express it this way because it also conveys that what it is attached to is like a cause motivating its object. Thus it is as if it were said: "Divorce for the sake of the waiting period." If it is for its sake, then it is known that the intention is to ease it upon the woman according to capacity, because the foundation of the religion is ease. This indicates that the waiting period is counted by purities, and that divorce during menstruation is forbidden, because a command to do something implies prohibition of its opposite. It does not indicate that the divorce is not effective, because a prohibition does not necessarily entail invalidity. All of this is clarified by the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding his divorce of his wife during menstruation, which was the occasion of revelation. The Prophet (ﷺ) became angry and ordered him to take her back, then keep her until she becomes pure, then if he wishes he may keep her, and if he wishes he may divorce her before touching her.

And He knew that the waiting period for those whose periods cannot be determined by menstrual cycles, namely the one not consummated, the one who has not menstruated, the post-menopausal woman, and the pregnant woman, has no sunna and no bid'a in their divorce. Likewise for the one who obtains divorce by khul' (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), because the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted Thabit ibn Qays, may Allah be pleased with him, to do khul' without inquiring about the state of his wife. This is because it generally arises from quarrel and the wife's request. The bid'i (innovated) divorce does take effect, because the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, to take her back, and he sins by it (p-142) after knowing. If he divorced during menstruation and then took her back, it is permissible for him to divorce her at the end of menstruation before intercourse. The command to keep her until the end of the purity and the menstruation that follows is for recommendation, so that it does not resemble one who takes back in order to divorce. There is no bid'a in divorcing three times together, because there is no indication of it in the verse nor in the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, which is its occasion. Yes, it may be claimed from the verse of al-Baqara in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾ [al-Baqara 2:229], and from the hadith, "Divorce is the most hated of lawful things to Allah," as narrated by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. So the most hateful of these to Him is the one most forbidden. And "He does not swear by it, nor does he seek to be sworn by it, except a hypocrite," as in al-Firdaws from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.

Since the Lawgiver's attention to the waiting period is strict, because it contains the ruling of deliberation in case of regret, and of certainty regarding the clearing of the womb, in order to protect lineages, and to cut off disputes and quarrels that lead to the loss of wealth and lives, and since the use of lam has implied this, He stated it explicitly in the form of a command, saying: ﴿And count﴾, meaning, keep an exact account, as if, in its precision, it were perceptible, after counting. ﴿the waiting period﴾, so that you complete it as three periods, as the command to do so was given previously, so that one knows the time of maintenance, of reconciliation, of residence, of the lawfulness of marrying the sister of the divorced woman, and similar other great benefits. Since divorce otherwise than in this manner is forbidden, because it is harmful and disobeys the command, and likewise negligence in counting, to the extent that a woman might be married before the waiting period ends, He commanded avoidance of all of that, saying: ﴿And fear﴾, meaning, in that regard, ﴿Allah﴾, meaning, the Supreme King to whom belongs creation and command by His essence (p-143), in time and in counting, because that involves what is His right. ﴿your Lord﴾, meaning, for His goodness in nurturing you, guiding you to the tolerant and easy monotheism, and removing all burdens from you.

Since He commanded taqwa and linked part of it to the attribute of goodness, He explained it by saying: ﴿Do not expel them﴾, meaning, O men, during the waiting period, ﴿from their houses﴾, meaning, the dwellings in which they were residing. He expressed it this way, perhaps to indicate that their entitlement to complete the waiting period in it is as great as the entitlement of an owner, and because they were in the state of marriage as if they were its owners. So it is not manly to show harshness by preventing them from it. And because if reconciliation occurs, she would be in the husband's possession and he would not have behaved badly in separating from her. And if that does not happen, and it becomes apparent that she is pregnant, there would be no doubt about the pregnancy.

Since that might be understood as being only for their right, He negated this by saying: ﴿nor shall they leave﴾, meaning, on their own accord if they wish to do so, without someone expelling them on the part of the husband or others. From this it is understood that completing the waiting period in the place of residence is obligatory, and that the provision of housing is upon the husband. She may go out for necessity, such as selling yarn, harvesting dates, and similar matters. Since the explicit meaning of this is that it is not permissible for him to expel her against her will, and it is not permissible for her to leave on her own while he is unwilling, it is understood from this that if both agree, it is permissible, because that falls outside what is forbidden. He made an exception to both sides of what is forbidden, saying:

(p-144) ﴿unless they commit﴾, meaning, the category of divorced women, which includes one and more, ﴿an obvious immorality﴾, meaning, a prohibited trait of extreme ugliness, ﴿clear﴾, meaning, manifest in itself, clearly evident to everyone to whom it is intended to be shown. This includes foul speech on her part toward the husband or his relatives, for it is like disobedience (nushuz), which forfeits her right to residence, so he may expel her to end the harm. This is the meaning of the reading of Ubayy, may Allah be pleased with him: "illa an yufhishna 'alaykum" (unless they commit indecency against you). It also includes adultery, so she may go out on her own, and others from the husband and elsewhere may expel her for the purpose of applying the prescribed punishment upon her and for other such immoralities, just as he may divorce her for disobedience, for then she has no right to residence.

Since the assumption was: these are the rulings of this branch, He followed it, to honour them, with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿These are﴾, meaning, these highly exalted rulings, with their majesty and their attribution to the Supreme King, from what has been mentioned in this surah and elsewhere, ﴿the limits of Allah﴾, meaning, the Supreme King who is the light of the heavens and the earth. Since the assumption was: whoever avoids them has truly been just to himself by taking the clear light, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And whoever transgresses﴾, meaning, whoever at any time deliberately sets out to exceed ﴿the limits of Allah﴾, meaning, the Supreme King, ﴿then he has wronged himself﴾ (p-145), by walking in darkness, so that he places things in other than their proper places. He thus becomes exposed to destruction through punishment, just as one walking in darkness is exposed to falling into a pit, stepping on a thorn, a snake, a scorpion, or a beast, or being isolated by a bandit, or losing the way to destructions from which escape is impossible. An example of this is a wise physician who prescribes a medicine according to a known formula, at a specified time and a specific place. If it is disobeyed, the disobedient one does not harm that physician; he harms only himself.

Since to Him belongs all creation under His commands, may He be glorified, and since all of them are good with no evil in them, in some hidden and deep aspects that cannot be grasped or counted, and since some of them may manifest as the tongue of misfortunes through the hand of power, and since the transgressor of them is a wrongdoer, and since among the clearest and nearest forms of such wrongdoing is falling into the abysses of passion, He explained this by saying, clarifying His greatness with an address of exaltation: ﴿You do not know﴾, meaning, O noble Prophet, what will result from that of matters which Allah brings about, so that you may counsel one who is absolutely (free) with something that would benefit him. Therefore, others are more deserving of this consideration.

Since He negated the knowledge of the unseen from him, because it is exclusive to Him, may He be glorified, and the object was omitted to emphasize generality, and since everyone, regarding what occurs to him of matters, is between hope and apprehension, He expressed this with a particle suitable for it, saying: ﴿Perhaps Allah﴾, meaning, He in whose hand are the hearts and the keys of all affairs (p-146), ﴿will bring about﴾, meaning, will create something new that did not exist, a lasting existence which creatures cannot cause to cease, so that it would extend throughout the duration of life. This is indicated by the omission of the preposition in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿after that﴾, meaning, after that new event, such as harm through expulsion, prolonging the waiting period, or other such things, ﴿some matter﴾, meaning, one of the important matters, such as an excessive desire for the wife. This cannot be accomplished if the harm was through triple divorce, or if she was of those with pride, and the wrongdoing affected her, and those who support her, so she refused herself to him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 65, verse 1 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said: When His statement preceded, ﴿O you who believe, let neither your wealth nor your children divert you from the remembrance of God﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9], and His statement in al-Taghabun, ﴿Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾ [al-Taghabun: 14], and His Exalted statement, ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15], and the believer may face what compels him to separate from one whom He has alerted to his trial and the gravity of his affliction, this surah came to alert to the manner of judgment in this separation and to clarify the rulings of divorce (talaq, the dissolution of marriage by the husband). It also shows that this enmity, however intense it becomes, and this fire of trial, however much it blazes, does not require complete disavowal and the severing of kindness, ﴿You do not know, perhaps God will bring about after that some matter﴾. God, glorified is He, enjoined generous kindness in general terms in His statement, (p-147) ﴿or release with kindness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229], and He explained the details of that and what relates to it. Thus this gentleness that is required is by pronouncing the divorce at the beginning of what the divorced woman prepares for in her waiting period ('iddah, the period a woman must observe after divorce or the death of her husband) and counts from its term, warning against pronouncing divorce during menstruation, which necessitates lengthening the 'iddah and increasing its duration. God, glorified is He, confirmed this with His statement, ﴿and fear God, your Lord﴾. Then God, glorified is He, drew attention to their right during the days of the 'iddah, namely that they remain in their residence from the time the divorce is pronounced until the end of the 'iddah, so He said, ﴿Do not expel them from their homes﴾, and so on, through what this surah continued with of explaining the rulings related to divorce and detailing all of that. And since children, when something appears from them that requires separating them and distancing them, do not need to be separated by anything other than rejection and abandonment, unlike the woman, they did not need what was needed in regard to women. Thus the reason for the revelation of the surah of Divorce in this position has become clear, and God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best. [End of quote.]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 65, verse 2:

When Allah, glorified is He, had defined what He does regarding the waiting period ('iddah), He followed it with what He does at its conclusion. He therefore made the command given within it the cause of what follows, expressing it with the particle of certainty (fa-idha), because the address is on the assumption that the husband is alive, informing that he has the right of return (raj'ah) up to the last part of the 'iddah. For if the return is established at its farthest end from the divorce, then what precedes it is more fitting, since it is closer to the divorce. So He said: ﴿When they reach their term﴾, that is, the divorced women, ﴿their term﴾, that is, they approach the end of the 'iddah with a great approach, ﴿then retain them﴾, that is, by taking them back. This indicates that the first (p-148) and second divorce is less than the irrevocable (ba'in), especially the third.

Since man, by reason of his deficiency, cannot attain perfect goodness, He said, in a manner of prohibition: ﴿with kindness﴾, that is, good companionship, not intending harm by another divorce to bring about a further waiting period, nor anything else. ﴿Or part from them﴾, that is, by not taking them back so that the 'iddah is completed and she may control herself, ﴿with kindness﴾, by fulfilling the right together with good speech and every matter which the Shari'ah recognized as good (ma'ruf), that is, made it beautiful. So he should not intend to harm her by separating her from her child, for example, or from him if she is beloved to him, for example, with the intention of harm alone and without any benefit, and likewise whatever resembles that of kinds of harm, by deed or by word. The verse has thus included, by its explicit wording, the urging to do good deeds, and by its implicit wording, the avoidance of forbidden things.

Since each of keeping and parting is a great matter, upon which rulings are built and whose opposites become forbidden, disagreement about them is of the utmost gravity. And since calling witnesses is most fitting to the intent and most decisive in ending dispute, Allah, Exalted is He, said, urging shrewdness, alertness, and distance from the actions of the heedless and the incapable: ﴿And call two witnesses﴾, that is, to the return or the parting, ﴿of just character﴾, that is, two responsible, free, trustworthy, alert persons, ﴿from among you﴾, that is, Muslims. This is a command of guidance, recommended. It is reported from al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that it is obligatory [in the revocable divorce], but the sound view is the first. Among its benefits is that neither of them dies and the other then claims the marriage continues, by the persistence of the bond of the 'iddah, in order to inherit.

Since giving testimony is difficult for the witness, because of neglecting his own duties and the difficulty of meeting the judge before whom it is to be given, and perhaps because of distance of place, and since justice in giving it also has obstacles, and since the witnesses are among those commanded to call witnesses, He urged giving testimony in the manner of justice by His saying: ﴿And establish the testimony﴾, that is, [O you who are commanded,] wherever you are witnesses, ﴿the testimony﴾, that is, which you have undertaken, by giving it in its most complete states, as one who intends to erect a thing so that it stands by itself, not needing anything to prop it up. And since perhaps one of those witnessed against may be inclined by some enticement, so that the witness gives it in favor of that thing and not because it is the truth, He said, encouraging and warning: ﴿for Allah﴾, that is, sincerely seeking the face of the Supreme King who encompasses everything in knowledge and power, He being the Lord of Majesty and Honor, in giving it in the manner of truth, outwardly and inwardly, not for the sake of the one in whose favor it is given nor the one against whom it is given, and with nothing sought except the face of Allah.

Since the rulings of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, especially in the Inimitable Book, are joined with their causes, and in them, upon reflection, are subtleties and fine points before which hearts humble themselves and within the breasts hearts tremble, He said: ﴿That﴾, that is, what I have mentioned (p-150) to you, O community, of these wondrously ordered matters of lofty purpose, and the most fitting of them here is calling witnesses and establishing the testimony.

Since the commands of Allah, the Exalted, His narratives, His rulings, and all His speech are distinguished among human speech by softening hearts and softening the restraining bridles, being a spirit in which is justice that souls desire, minds love, and natures incline to, and by which the heavens and the earth stand, and since in it is also the mention of those whom upright natures love from all the people of goodness, among the prophets, the angels, and the saints, along with the honoring of all by the mention of Allah, it is called admonition (wa'z). It is expressed in the passive form to indicate that admonition in itself is beneficial even if its speaker is not known, and to indicate that the agent is known to be Allah, since it is called admonition though it consists of rulings. So He said: ﴿by which is admonished﴾, that is, is softened and made tender, ﴿whoever is﴾, that is, firmly established, from all people, ﴿believing in Allah﴾, that is, who brings about and renews, among you and others, on a continuous basis, from the core of his heart, belief in the King to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿and the Last Day﴾. Since the Resurrection is the focal point of wisdom, because this world is a field for the Hereafter, and there is no sowing without harvest, the absence of belief in it nullifies faith. So He said: ﴿and the Last Day﴾, for it is the greatest focal point for softening hearts. As for one who is not characterized by this, his heart is hardened, so that he is not admonished by it, because he never benefits from it.

Since worship is not performed except with help, and the implied meaning is: whoever takes admonition from this, his taking admonition is a witness to his belief in this, and he is God-fearing, He followed it with the parenthetical statement between these rulings, to emphasize the encouragement toward the help which results from piety: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾, that is, reveres the Supreme King, so that he places between himself and what angers Him a shield from what pleases Him, which is bringing about what He commanded and avoiding what He forbade, of divorce and other matters, outwardly and inwardly. That is righteousness, strong in knowledge of faith and in acting by performing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden, because it has preceded that when piety stands alone in the Qur'an without an accompanying term, it covers both command and prohibition, and when it is joined with other terms, such as ihsan or ridwan, it specifies prohibitions. ﴿He will make for him an exit﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, by means of piety will make for him, by repelling harms, an escape from every constriction that surrounds him, in return for what he has avoided of the prohibitions.

﴿And He provides for him﴾ by His power and might, by bringing him benefit in religion, in this world, and in the Hereafter, in return for what he has obtained by carrying out the commands.

Since the sweetest gifts are those that come from a source one does not expect, He said: ﴿from where he does not expect﴾, that is, from where his hope does not reach. He emphasized and magnified the promise here, because although it is general for every God-fearing person, its connection to what came before is stronger. The discussion before this point concerned the rights of people, the strictness regarding them is greater, and the motives to violate them are more powerful. Therefore, guarding oneself in this matter means not divorcing during menstruation, not harming the woman by prolonging the waiting period (p-152) or by expelling her from the dwelling, not concealing testimony, not making its performance difficult, not neglecting any part of it. Because of this, and because of the anxiety that human beings are naturally disposed to feel about their affairs, the promise is stressed and emphasized. Upon this He added: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah﴾, that is, who leans on Him in all his affairs, entrusting them to Him and depending on Him, ﴿upon Allah﴾, that is, the King in whose hand is everything, and there is none comparable to Him. Thus the verse combines the three pillars without which reliance (tawakkul) is not valid: all-encompassing knowledge, so that one is not deceived; complete power, so that He is not incapable; and mercy and care for the one who relies upon Him, so that He does not wrong him. Reliance is accompanied by taking the means, and it is one of the great spiritual stations. Otherwise it would be mere dependence, which is not a station at all, but rather lowness of aspiration and lack of manliness, since it nullifies the wisdom of Allah which He established in this world through the arrangement of effects upon causes. This is what al-Malawi said. ﴿then He is sufficient for him﴾, that is, Allah, in the unseen of the unseen, let alone the seen, by reason of his reliance upon Him. The object of the verb is omitted for generality, and the preposition indicating elevation (ʿalā, "upon") is used to indicate that he has placed all his affairs upon Him, glorified is He, because He is the Strong whom nothing can resist, the Generous who handles these matters and looks after them well, the Mighty who repels from him every harm and brings him every benefit, and other great meanings. Thus nothing appears to him in the world of witnessing that would make him wretched, neither from the unseen nor from the unseen of the unseen. In a hadith:

"If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance He is due, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening." (p-153)

Since this is a matter that imagination can hardly encompass, He explained it with a statement that magnifies it, using emphasis and explicit naming in place of a pronoun: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing every perfection, free of every flaw of deficiency, ﴿will accomplish His purpose﴾, that is, all that He wills. It must take effect, whether or not reliance is present. He called it "affair" (amr) to indicate that it is something deserving of being commanded, and to indicate that when He wills existence, it is not delayed in any way; rather it is like a lowly subject receiving an order from the great and exalted King.

Since the decreeing of destinies by the All-Powerful requires that nothing in them be neglected, He gave as the reason what necessitates the certainty of the promise and of reliance, saying: ﴿Allah has set﴾, that is, the King who has no equal and whose judgment none can repel, a setting that is absolute, without restriction to any aspect or condition, ﴿for everything a measure﴾, that is, a determination that does not exceed it in its quantity, its time, its place, all its accidents and states, even if all creatures strive to exceed it. Whoever relies upon Him gains reward and has his pain lightened, and tranquility is cast into his heart. Whoever does not rely upon Him, that does not benefit him; his pain increases and his distress is prolonged by the intensity of his striving and the failure of the means which he believes to be the bringers of success. Whoever is content, for him is contentment; whoever is angry, for him is anger. The pen has dried, so nothing is added to the destinies, nor is anything subtracted from them. (p-154)

It is related that a man came to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "Appoint me to something of what Allah has given you authority over." He said: "Do you recite the Qur'an?" He said: "No." He said: "We do not appoint one who does not recite the Qur'an." So the man left and strove until he learned the Qur'an, hoping to return to ʿUmar and be appointed. When he had learned the Qur'an, he stayed away from ʿUmar. ʿUmar saw him one day and said: "O you! Have you abandoned us?" He said: "O Commander of the Believers! I am not one who abandons. But I learned the Qur'an, and Allah made me independent of ʿUmar and of the door of ʿUmar." He said: "Which verse made you independent?" He said: the Most High's saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ [al-Talaq: 2] ﴿and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾. End.

Whoever relies upon anyone other than Him, glorified and exalted is He, is lost, because that other does not know the interests; and even if he knows them, he does not know where they are; and even if he knows where they are, he does not know when to employ them; and even if he knows when, he does not know how much quantity is to be employed; and even if he knows how much, he does not know how to employ them. He, glorified is He, is the One singled out with the knowledge of all of that, and what He knows in its true knowledge, none else knows.

The verse implies that whoever does not fear Allah will have his provision restricted, and this agrees with what Ibn Ḥibbān narrated in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and al-Ḥākim, and the wording is his, and he said: its chain is sound, from Thawbān, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: (p-155) The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nothing repels the decree except supplication, and nothing increases the lifespan except righteousness, and a man is indeed deprived of provision because of a sin he commits." It also implies that whoever does not rely upon Him will not be sufficed in anything.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 65, verse 4:

When he placed these admonitory sentences in the middle of the numbers, as an indication of their greatness and an incitement to act upon them and hasten to them, and concluded with "al-taqdir" (the determination), he followed that with an explanation of the quantities of the waiting period, in a manner that made clear that the preceding discourse concerned women who could be returned to (al-hawa'id al-raj'iyyat). So He said: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾, i.e., of the divorced women, ﴿of menstruation﴾, i.e., of menstruation (al-hayd) and its time, because they have reached an age that exceeds the span in which women hope for menstruation, so that they are no longer in a state of hoping for it. That age is fifty-five years, or sixty years; it was also said seventy years, and these are the qawa'id (those who have ceased). As for the one whose menstruation has stopped in a period in which she still hopes for menstruation, she waits until the age of despair (sinn al-ya's).

Since this ruling is specific to the wives of Muslims, because of the sanctity of their marital bed (furush) and the preservation of their lineages, He said: ﴿of your women﴾, i.e., O Muslims, whether they are Muslims or from the People of the Book. Since what necessitates the waiting period (al-'iddah) is actually consummation (al-dukhul) and not merely divorce, He said: ﴿if you are in doubt﴾, by your delaying the consideration of their affair, which leads you to doubt [whether -] whether they are pregnant or not; and this is by entering upon them, which is the cause of suspicion of pregnancy in general. ﴿Then their waiting period is three months﴾, each month standing in place of a menstrual cycle (hayda), because the usual custom of women is that each qur' (period) falls in a month.

When he had completed the two categories of those who menstruate, by allusion and by explicit statement, he said: ﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾, i.e., because of their young age, or because they have no menstruation at all, even if they are adults; their waiting period is likewise three months. This indicates that those who do menstruate, whether they are irrevocably divorced or not, have a waiting period of three qur', as was mentioned earlier in al-Baqarah, because these months are a substitute for it. Then the qur' (which is purity) is either between two menstrual periods, or between the divorce and the menstruation. All of this concerns the divorced woman. As for the widow whose husband has died, her period is four months and ten days, as in al-Baqarah.

When he finished with the women past menstruation who are pregnant, he followed it with mention of pregnant women, and said: ﴿And for those who are pregnant﴾, i.e., of all wives, Muslim and disbelieving, divorced in every case, and widowed when their pregnancy is from the husband, whether he is Muslim or not, ﴿their term﴾, i.e., the end of the waiting period, whether or not they have menstruation along with the pregnancy, ﴿is that they lay down﴾. Since the singular "hamal" (pregnancy) does not give rise to confusion, and since the plural might suggest that none of them is lawfully free until all of them have given birth, He said: ﴿their burden﴾. This is general in its scope, but specified by the verse ﴿who wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 234], because preserving the generality of this verse is more appropriate than preserving the generality of "azwajan" in the other, since the generality of this one is inherent (bi'l-dhat), as the relative pronoun is among the forms of generality, while the generality of "azwajan" is incidental (bi'l-'arad), since it is a distributive term that cannot encompass all wives in one state. The ruling here is also causally linked to the attribute of pregnancy, unlike the other. Also, Subay'ah bint al-Harith gave birth to her child a few nights after her husband's death, and the Prophet ﷺ permitted her to marry. And because this verse was revealed later than the verse of al-Baqarah, giving it precedence over that one is specification (takhsis), while giving precedence to that one in acting upon its generality is abrogation (raf') of the ruling contained in the specific; so it is naskh (abrogation). The first is the preponderant view, due to consensus upon it. If the pregnancy is from fornication or from a doubtful union, it has no sanctity, and the waiting period is by menstruation.

Since the affairs of women in companionship and separation, in ease and hardship, involve extreme difficulty, and nothing motivates justice and chastity in them except the fear of God, He repeated, as an embellishment, the exhortation to taqwa (God-consciousness), as an allusion to that and an encouragement to adhere to what He, glorified is He, has set as limits. So He said, connecting it to what is implied in the context: whoever does not observe these limits, God makes his affairs difficult: ﴿And whoever fears God﴾, i.e., fear of the Supreme King is continuously present, so that He places between Himself and His wrath a shield through obedience to Him, seeking what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden, ﴿He will make for him﴾, i.e., it will be continuously made so, by the continuity of taqwa ("Indeed God does not tire until you tire") ﴿from his affair﴾, i.e., all of it, in marriage and otherwise, ﴿ease﴾, i.e., facility, relief, and good in both abodes, through averting harm and gaining benefit; and this is greater than the mere way out mentioned in the first verse.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 65, verse 5:

When the repeated exhortation to (taqwa) God-consciousness came in order to answer a question about its cause, he resumed with his words as a rationale for it: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the matter mentioned of all these supremely elevated rulings, ﴿is the command of God﴾, i.e., the Supreme King to whom all perfection belongs, and he drew attention to the high rank of the command with his words: ﴿He has sent it down to you﴾. Since the implied sense is: whoever is led astray by desire into the abysses of ruin, down to the lowest of the low, he followed it with his words: ﴿And whoever fears God﴾, i.e., the One with whom no one has any command to bring about or to avert, and since man is a locus of weakness and deficiency, he gave him comfort in that if a lapse occurs from him, then returning to Him through taqwa is a kindness toward him, and in it is a reward for his taqwa, through warding off and benefit. So He said: ﴿He will remove from him﴾, i.e., He will cover over with a great covering, conceal, hide, and cause to fall away, ﴿his misdeeds﴾, all of ﴿his misdeeds﴾, so that he may be free of what distances him, for good deeds do away with misdeeds. And since the Generous does not content Himself with merely pardoning one who turns to Him, He said: ﴿and will magnify his reward﴾, by transforming his misdeeds into good deeds and paying him their reward in both abodes, multiplied, so that he is adorned with what brings nearness. This is greater than the general ease mentioned earlier.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 65, verse 6:

When He had mentioned the expiation (takfir) and followed it with the great reward, and the obligation to leave the divorced woman in the house of divorce had preceded, along with His permission to expel them upon a manifest immorality, and since the house of divorce might be borrowed and was not fitting for the husband, and since the preceding speech may have come down upon him, He resumed the explanation for him in a manner that admits no ambiguity. So He said, commanding after that prohibition, in a way that points by what precedes it and what follows it to forbearance toward them in what forbearance is possible, preserving hearts and removing discord after the alienation brought by divorce, lest the breaking and the estrangement grow great: ﴿House them﴾, that is, these separated women, during the ʿiddah (waiting period), whether they are divorced women who are pregnant or not, whether they are irrevocably divorced (mabtutat) or revocably divorced (raj'iyyat), in contrast to the ʿiddah due to death without pregnancy, or one that arises from a doubtful union (shubhah) or from annulment (faskh).

And since what is meant is a dwelling fitting for them, even if it is only part of the man's dwelling, He introduced the particle of partiality and said: ﴿from where you dwell﴾, that is, from the places where you live, so that it will be near you, so that your attending to them for protection and the meeting of their needs will be easy.

And since a person may have dwelt in past times in what he is no longer able to afford, He said, clarifying the dwelling commanded, while preserving affection by not imposing what is burdensome: ﴿according to your means﴾, that is, your ability and capacity, by rent, or ownership, or lending, until the ʿiddah ends, whether by pregnancy or otherwise. And since housing may be accompanied by animosity, He said: ﴿and do not harm them﴾, that is, while they dwell in the dwelling or elsewhere. And since harm may be for a good purpose, by way of discipline for a matter that is right, so that through an apparent small evil one reaches a great good, He said: ﴿to constrict them﴾, that is, constriction to an extreme degree with no doubt that it is such, imposed ﴿upon them﴾, until it compels them to go out. And since maintenance is obligatory for the revocably divorced woman, and her ʿiddah is sometimes by menstrual cycles, sometimes by months, and sometimes by pregnancy, and since one might suppose that maintenance is not obligatory for the period beyond the three months for a pregnant revocably divorced woman, and for the entire period for others, He said: ﴿And if they are pregnant﴾, that is, the women in ʿiddah, ﴿with child﴾, that is, from their husbands, whatever the ʿiddah is, whether from death, irrevocable divorce, or revocable divorce, ﴿then spend upon them﴾, even if the months have passed, ﴿until they give birth to their burden﴾, for the cause is the ʿiddah by pregnancy. This conditional clause indicates that among the irrevocably divorced women in ʿiddah, only the pregnant ones are singled out for the obligation of maintenance.

And since Glorified is He made the obligation of maintenance end with delivery, and since she may wish to nurse her child, and her occupation with nursing him would cause her to forgo many of her aims and would break her, He consoled her by saying, urging the matching of kindness with kindness among the spouses, and indicating by the particle of doubt that nursing is not obligatory upon her: ﴿And if they nurse for you﴾. He made clear that the child belongs to the men by His words, may He be exalted: ﴿for you﴾, that is, for a wage after the bond of marriage has been severed: ﴿then give them their wages﴾ for that nursing. And since matters concerning women, such as this, are a locus of dispute, especially the matter of nursing, and since the danger in its matter is great, and since God Most High has shown mercy to this community by stirring up for each of two contending parties someone who commands them to what is good, especially regarding the child, out of mercy toward him, He said, indicating this: ﴿and confer among yourselves﴾, that is, let some of you command others concerning nursing and its wage and other matters, and let some of you accept the command of others. He increased their eagerness in this by His words: ﴿among yourselves﴾, that is, this good does not go beyond you. He emphasized this by His words: ﴿in an acceptable manner﴾, and He made it indefinite, affirming for the community contentment with what is within reach, which is achieved with creation through fairness, with the self through opposition to its desires, and with the Truth through acknowledgment.

And since that necessitates ease, and since among people there may be found those in whom evil predominates, He said, indicating by the expression of doubt that although this is found, it is rare, connecting it to what is implied, namely: if you are at ease, then that is your good fortune, and you are deserving of hearing this promise for it: ﴿But if you are at odds﴾, that is, each of you seeks from the other what is difficult for the other, such as the woman seeking a wage while the husband seeks her nursing without payment; then he has no right to compel her.

And since Glorified has undertaken the provision of His servants and decreed it before bringing them into existence, He said, informing, as a consolation to the father, with what is fitting as a rebuke to the mother: ﴿then another will nurse for him﴾ (i.e., with a promise that does not fail), and He turned the address to the third person, announcing that the father has abandoned what is preferable in what he is worthy of, namely ease, since he is fit to be more generous in expenditure and greater in standing than to be constrained regarding what the woman is content with, following the example of the Prophet (ﷺ) in that: "He was never given a choice between two matters without choosing the easier of them, so long as it was not sinful or a severance of kinship." He said: ﴿for him﴾, that is, for the father, ﴿another﴾, that is, a wet-nurse other than the mother, and God will suffice him for her; and he has no right to compel her, unless the child will not accept the breast of anyone else. This ruling is not restricted to the divorced woman but applies likewise to the wife still under the marriage.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 65, verse 7:

Since hardship (al-mu'asarah) in most cases results from withholding generosity (al-samaha), and withholding generosity comes from fear of destitution, He, glorified is He, drew attention to the fact that this is not an excuse, by dividing people into one who is granted abundance and others. Moreover, it is most fitting for one who is granted abundance to be generous and not to think ill of his Lord, since he has tested His bounty. And the one whose provision is restricted should not act like one who fears that He will fail to fulfil His promise. So He said, explaining ease (al-muyassarah): ﴿Let the one of abundance spend from his abundance﴾, meaning from wealth that is ample. He did not require of him all of his capacity, but said: ﴿from his abundance﴾, which is the abundance that Allah has granted him. And since giving without measure necessarily implies abundance, measuring (al-taqdir) became a metaphor for restriction, so He said: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted﴾, meaning constricted, his movement is confined and his livelihood is stilled, ﴿upon him⦆ his provision, by Allah making him, the One who alone can restrict and expand, unable to have anything beyond his basic necessities alone, without (p-١٦٣) any surplus for anything other than them, for a matter among the matters through which Allah shows the helplessness of His servants, out of mercy towards them, so that He may refine their souls through it. He used the passive form to teach courtesy towards Him, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿let him spend﴾, meaning it is obligatory upon the nursing mother and others, from everything that Allah has made obligatory upon him or recommended to him. Glorified and exalted is He promised that He does not leave anyone without something with which to sustain himself as long as he lives, by His saying, indicating by the partitive that what He has made obligatory does not exhaust what He has bestowed: ﴿from what Allah has given him﴾, meaning the King who does not exhaust what He has, and whose generosity has no limit, even if it be from capital, from the household furnishings, or from the price of a property if he has no income from it, because He, glorified is He, has guaranteed replacement, and from the possession of what suffices him for the present time. Then, if he is anxious for an increase for tomorrow, that is an anxiety that is not merciful, and its bearer is not helped. In this is guidance to follow his example (ﷺ) in avoiding excessive effort and in ease in every matter according to the circumstances.

Since He, exalted is He, has the right to impose what cannot be borne, He informed that He has shown mercy to His servants by not doing so. So He said, giving the reason or beginning a new statement as an answer to one who says: what does one do who has nothing at all? Making the religion of (ﷺ) beloved for what it contains of ease: ﴿Allah does not burden any soul﴾, meaning the One who possesses perfection in attributes of mercy and of bestowing favour upon us by lightening the burden, ﴿beyond what He has given it﴾, meaning any soul whatsoever. Perhaps this implies that whoever is required to spend finds from his surplus what fills his need of the surplus of goods (p-١٦٤) beyond satisfying his hunger and covering his nakedness.

Since mention of destitution may be more painful, He, exalted is He, said, consoling him and soothing his heart, urging belief in the unseen: ﴿Allah will bring after hardship⦆ meaning the King, who possesses all perfection, so there is no failure in His promise, and He omitted the preposition for emphasis in the statement, and said: ﴿after hardship﴾, meaning after the matters that have become difficult, not that He makes this after every hardship. ﴿ease﴾, meaning there is no escape from this, and no one exists whose restriction continues throughout his life in all his circumstances. Al-Qushayri said: waiting for ease from Allah is the attribute of those in the middle states, who have fallen short of the rank of contentment, and for whom the existence and absence of the cause are equal, and who have risen above the limit of despair and hopelessness, and live in the expanses of hope, and console themselves with the goodness of promises. End of quotation. Allah has indeed fulfilled His promise to those who were alive when the verse was revealed, for He granted them the whole of the Arabian Peninsula, then Persia and Byzantium, and they plundered their treasures until they became the wealthiest of people. The truth of the verse is perpetual, but it was more evident among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, because their faith was more complete.

When the command had reached its fullest extent in legal rulings, admonitions, and encouragement for those who obey, nothing remained but the warning to those who disobey, through what has been witnessed of exemplary punishments and severe penalties. For among people is the dullard who takes no lesson from what he sees. The implied construction was: "How many people there were who were in the utmost hardship and then obeyed Our commands, so We placed them in the utmost ease, indeed We made them kings." This was joined to it as a caution against comfort, since comfort mostly leads to transgression, and as a threat to the people of disobedience. His words, indicating the multitude of towns that exceeded all bounds, are: ﴿How many a town﴾, meaning a great, populous city, and he referred to its people by the city itself as hyperbole. ﴿Transgressed﴾, meaning they became arrogant and went beyond the limit in their disobedience and tyranny, so they turned away out of obstinacy ﴿from the command of their Lord﴾, meaning the One who had done good to them, and none other does good to them, through abundance of provision, pleasant living, gentleness in nurture and mercy, after bringing them into existence and granting them dominion ﴿and His messengers﴾. So they did not accept from them what the messengers brought them from God, for obedience to them is obedience to God.

When the reckoning of such people was [for destruction], because reckoning means mentioning deeds and recompensing each one with what it deserves, He said, turning to the station of speech in the manifestation of majesty: ﴿So We reckoned with it﴾, meaning that as a consequence of their not being grateful for the kindness, We counted their deeds. Since this was in the manner of close scrutiny (munaqasha), down to the speck and the thread, with recompense for each act befitting it, He said: ﴿a severe reckoning﴾, in its literal sense of mentioning all deeds and recompensing them. This is the scrutiny: when the doer leaves an effect through his deed, like an engraving on a hard object, the one who recompenses leaves an effect upon him in accordance with his deed, thoroughly and exhaustively. As for an easy reckoning, it is merely the presentation of deeds without recompense for their evil, which is an implicational indication (dalalat tadammun). He specified this town for severity because its turning away was of this kind, as indicated by calling it "transgression" (utuww). ﴿And We punished it﴾, meaning in this world, as recompense for the sins We had counted, ﴿with a terrible punishment﴾, meaning one of extreme strangeness, because the intellect is bewildered by its matter, since it has not seen its like nor anything close to it by which to take warning. Mentioning the multitude removed the suspicion that the destruction had occurred by mere chance at some time.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 65, verse 9:

﴿So she tasted﴾ as a consequence of that, after she had possessed abundance and strength, ﴿the evil﴾ — that is, the bad outcome, punishment, severity, heaviness and corruption ﴿of her affair﴾ — that is, in her insolence and in everything she used to conspire over. He likened it to a pasture that is unwholesome, which sickens and destroys (its grazers).

Since every person who is subdued consoles himself by awaiting relief and hoping for a good end, He removed this hope, using the masculine form of the verb to indicate severity, saying: ﴿And the consequence of her affair was﴾ — that is, its final result, its termination and its aftermath, in all of her deeds in which she used to be ﴿loss﴾ — that is, pure loss in both abodes. Thus, whenever the matter is prolonged, they find it before them; for whoever sows thorns, as al-Qushayri said, does not reap roses, and whoever neglects the right of Allah is not obeyed in his own share, and whoever is burned by opposing the command of Allah, let him endure the suffering of the punishment of Allah. Then he explained the loss, or resumed the answer for one who says: "Does she have anything other than this in this world?", with His saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 65, verse 10:

﴿Allah has prepared﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, ﴿for them﴾, after death and after resurrection, ﴿a severe punishment﴾.

When the rulings and their proofs were complete, and the verses and their concluding phrases were firmly established, and the warnings and their dangers were set forth, their summation and the fruit of their context and admonition were what follows from His statement, the Exalted, alerting to what gives life a good existence and delivers in both abodes: ﴿So fear Allah﴾, i.e., He to whom all command belongs, by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

Since extracting the admonitions from the rulings and deriving them from the concluding phrases of this discourse is a great matter, of such subtlety that none perceive it except those of understanding, the Exalted said: ﴿O people of understanding﴾, i.e., the pure intellects that penetrate from the outward to the inward, ﴿who have believed﴾, i.e., who have emerged from the circle of polytheism and truly brought faith into being. Then He gave the reason for this command with what removes all excuse, saying, alerting to what He has bestowed upon us of correspondence (al-muraslah), for the correspondence of the great is a source of pride, so how much more the correspondence of kings, and how much more the correspondence of the King of kings, urging thereby gratitude to Him: ﴿Allah has indeed sent down﴾, i.e., He to whom belong the attributes of perfection, ﴿to you﴾ specifically, ﴿a reminder﴾, i.e., a complete discourse, mentioned, in which is the utmost honor for everyone who accepts it. Rather, the whole earth has been honored by its descent, the punishment has been lifted from it, and light has covered it. And the truth is that in it is the clarification of everything; whoever seeks its light is guided, and whoever takes refuge in the cool of its shade reaches, from the disease of ignorance, its cure.

The Messenger ﷺ is the embodiment of the Surah of the Qur'an: the Qur'an is his inward reality and he is its outward manifestation, since he is its creation and has no speech or act except through it, so he is as though he were it. Therefore the phrase ﴿a Messenger﴾ is put in apposition (badal) to the word ﴿a reminder﴾, the matter being clear enough that it needs no interpretation. In the language, the word al-dhikr (الذِّكْر), with a kasra on the dhal, means, as stated in al-Qamus (the dictionary al-Qamus al-Muhit), a man who is strong, brave and noble. Then he explained that it is a reminder by saying ﴿reciting﴾, meaning following up and relating to ﴿you the verses of Allah﴾, meaning the proofs of the Greatest King, Possessor of Majesty and Honour, which are most manifest, while they are ﴿clarifying﴾, meaning that there is no ambiguity in them in any way. (p-١٦٩) Since it has become clear that the Reminder and the Messenger are one thing, and he knew the honour contained in this sending, he followed this with the explanation of another honour by stating the fruit of its sending down, saying: ﴿that He may bring out those who believe﴾, meaning those who affirmed the two testimonies (al-shahadatayn), ﴿and do﴾ righteous deeds as confirmation of what they said with their tongues and as realisation of it from their hearts, ﴿the righteous deeds﴾ from among actions, ﴿from the darknesses﴾, meaning the darkness of the soul and the blameworthy character traits that lead to the darkness of the limbs through their doing of wrongdoing and their scattering along satanic paths, ﴿to the light﴾, the spiritual, intellectual light, pure and free from any taint, by following the path of Allah, which is [one -] without dispersion in it and clear without ambiguity in it. ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow the [other] ways﴾ [al-An'am: 153], just as they hastened to bring themselves out of the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith, and from the corruption of righteous deeds [to the rectitude of righteous deeds -]. This is by making them take on the character of the Qur'an, so that they become a manifestation [of it -] in their movements, their stillnesses, their words and their actions, and thus they become a reminder.

Since the implied sense is: whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds witnesses the blessings of that in himself immediately, he followed it with a statement of the happiness of the Hereafter, His saying, exalted is He: (p-١٧٠) ﴿And whoever believes in Allah﴾, meaning renews continually and constantly the faith in the Supreme King, by never ceasing to be ascending in the ladders of his knowledge, ﴿and acts﴾ with continuous renewal ﴿righteously﴾ for Allah and in Allah. For him is perpetual bounty, and this is the meaning of His making him enter the Garden. Since it had previously been mentioned, shortly before, in the verse of taqwa, that He would remove from him his misdeeds, He said, explaining His saying ﴿and magnify for him a reward﴾ [al-Talaq: 5]: ﴿He will admit him﴾, meaning immediately, figuratively, through what He grants him of the delights of gnosis, and what He opens for him of intimacy, and in the Hereafter in reality, into ﴿Gardens﴾, meaning orchards which are at the utmost of what can be in gathering [-all] trees and the beauty of the abode. He joined the continuity of their irrigation by His saying ﴿flowing﴾, and the openness of much of their ground by His saying ﴿beneath them﴾, meaning beneath their chambers, ﴿rivers﴾; or it is a metaphor (kinayah) that their land is in the utmost of irrigation, such that its dweller flows in whatever place he wishes [a river, and -]. To increase its greatness, the reading of Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir with the nun of majesty (nun al-'azamah) indicated it.

Since He made the condition and the answer singular, following the wording of "man" (من), as an indication that neither faith nor its reward requires the partnership of anyone [in -], and that acceptance is not contingent on anything other than the described attribute, He combined the state as good news (p-١٧١) that those who enter are many, and that the one who enters the abode of honour will never suffer humiliation thereafter at all. So He said: ﴿abiding therein﴾, and He emphasised the meaning of eternal abiding so that perpetuity without end might be understood, so He said: ﴿forever﴾. And since He made known that eternal abiding is for all who enter the Garden, He returned to the first style, specifying each individual, to express the greatness of this reward, by His saying, as a consequence of that, alerting that this consequence is one whose statement should be expected from everyone who hears this good news: ﴿Allah has indeed made good provision for him﴾, meaning the Supreme King, Possessor of Majesty and Honour, ﴿for him﴾, meaning specifically, ﴿a provision﴾, meaning great and wondrous. Al-Qushayri said: Good provision is what is sufficient, without deficiency, such that one is not distracted from his affairs by it, nor is it an excess that preoccupies him from enjoying what he has been provided, out of greed; likewise the provisions of hearts: the best of them is that he has of the states what suffices him without deficiency, and he is not tormented by his thirst, nor is it an excess whereby he is at risk of delusions from which he does not emerge except by a heavenly support from Allah.

The Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 65, Verse 12:

Since he had previously mentioned the benefit of the remembrance (dhikr) as conveying (naql) from one creation to another, and since it is well known that moving a mountain from its place is easier than moving a person from his created nature and condition, and since it had been stated earlier that the reward for striving in that matter is the described Gardens, and since that requires complete power, He indicated His exalted power over it by His saying: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection, of which all-encompassing power is one. Then He informed about Him with that which indicates it, because the craft points to the craftsman and to the attributes he has, so He said: ﴿Who created﴾, that is, brought into existence alone from non-existence by His power, in accordance with what He arranged by His knowledge, in this wondrous and near pattern, ﴿seven heavens﴾, that is, and they witness the greatness of that and bear witness that none can do it except one of perfect knowledge and complete power. Then He added to that what you know better, saying: ﴿and of the earth the like thereof﴾, that is, seven, as indicated by the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) in the Two Sahihs: "Whoever takes a span of land unjustly, it will be hung around his neck from seven earths." The wording of Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) is: "He will be swallowed down with it on the Day of Resurrection to seven earths." What is useful in this has been mentioned previously in Surah al-Sajdah. Its apparent meaning indicates that just as they are equal in number, so they are equal in roundness and in each one encompassing the one beneath it, and that the one we are on is the uppermost seventh, like the seventh heaven whose ceiling is the Kursi, because that is more indicative of what the context requires of complete knowledge and all-encompassing power in deducing it. By His saying: ﴿The command descends﴾, that is, gradually, ﴿among them﴾, the command which the All-Merciful bestows of governance, of religious matters and of creation, from the 'Arsh and the Kursi, ﴿among them﴾ by revelation from the uppermost seventh heaven to the lowest seventh earth, while you see them without gaps. So He penetrated among them until He passed through them. And that, Allah knows best, is what He wills of His great governance: sending down Books, dispatching Messengers, establishing one Law and abrogating another, directing causes toward their effects, such as rain and plants, night and day, the seasons, the creation of animals, minerals and all kinds of plants, and the angels' transmission of all created things. This is what the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah indicate. Some have interpreted it to mean that they are seven regions (aqalim), and this is rejected, since according to the principle that interpretation without evidence is play, in light of the explicit prophetic hadith that follows. The discourse that governs what is interpreted and what is not is that transmitted texts are of four types: definitive in transmission and in indication; speculative in both; speculative in transmission but definitive in indication; and the reverse, definitive in transmission but speculative in indication. The first must be believed in its apparent meaning, and whoever opposes it disbelieves. The rest require believing their apparent meanings so long as they are not contradicted. If they are contradicted by something definitive, it is obligatory to depart from the apparent meaning by consensus (ijma'), and whoever believes otherwise disbelieves. Then, after that, people hold two positions. As for the early generations (salaf), they entrust the intended meaning to Allah the Exalted. As for the later scholars (khalaf), if there is one single possible meaning, they specify it; if there are several possible meanings, they list them without specifying any of them, while acknowledging that they are not certain that the intended meaning is any of what they have mentioned, but that it is something fitting to the context, and that knowledge of it is with Allah. And they hold that the way of the salaf is closer and safer, and that what led them to interpretation was only the spread of innovators and their publicizing of their innovation among people. Imam 'Ala' al-Din al-Qawnawi (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him), in the chapter on the Sirah of his commentary al-Hawi, said: The Imam, meaning Imam al-Haramayn, said: "If people had remained in the purity of Islam as they were, we would not have made the occupation with the science of kalam obligatory; rather we might have forbidden it. But now, since innovations have arisen, there is no way to leave them, their waves surging, so it is necessary to prepare what can call to the right path and dissolve doubts. Thus, engaging with rational proofs and resolving doubts has become a collective obligation (fard kifayah). Whoever doubts any principle of belief must strive to remove that doubt until his creed is sound." End of quotation.

Then you will find that scholars differ regarding some of the proofs: some take them according to their apparent meaning and some interpret them. This is due to the disagreement over whether the opposing evidence is definitive in indication or not. This place is part of that, because the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah indicate that the earths are like the heavens in number, in that between them there is emptiness, and in that in each one there are creatures that no one knows except Allah. Indeed, some reports almost amount to certainty in this matter, but it has not moved beyond being speculative. Most scholars and their verifiers hold that the opposing evidence, which is what the astronomers (ahl 'ilm al-hay'a) have said of the proofs that it is one, is not definitive. So they interpreted the number seven as referring to the seven regions. However, I have seen in the matter of plurality (ta'addud) a clear hadith, but I do not know its status. Ibn Burjan mentioned it under the Name of Allah, al-Malik, in his commentary on the Beautiful Names, saying that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what is beneath this earth?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Water. Do you know what is beneath that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Air. Do you know what is beneath that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Earth. Do you know what is beneath that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." Until he counted seven earths.

Then I saw it in al-Tirmidhi from Abu Razin al-'Uqayli, and its wording is: "Do you know what is beneath you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the earth." Then he said: "Do you know what is beneath that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Beneath it is another earth, and between them is five hundred years." Until he counted seven earths, between each earth is a journey of five hundred years.

Then I saw in al-Firdaws from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The distance between the heaven and the heaven is five hundred years' journey, and the breadth of each heaven and its thickness is five hundred years. The distance between the seventh heaven and the Kursi and the 'Arsh is similar to that. The distance between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years, and the earths, their breadth and their thickness are similar to that."

When He mentioned the craft, Exalted is He, as an alert to reflecting upon it and taking lessons from it, He mentioned that its fruit is knowledge of His attributes, after the incapacity to encompass knowledge of His Essence, Exalted is He. So He said: ﴿That you may know﴾, that is, through this world which He brought into existence, with the arrangement of each of the two categories as seven, each one with a great distance between it and the other, together with the additional density, and you know that a body, especially a dense one, is not separated from another like it except by a Separator who is overpowering with a dazzling might, a manifest power, and all-encompassing knowledge of what that requires. How much more so when it is upon this wondrous method and impregnable form, enduring through the ages and eras, the succession of months and years, according to a known reckoning and a well-ordered system, which only the most accomplished in reckoning and the most correct in judgment can grasp. Together with the benefits that overflow to its inhabitants, and the conveniences that glorify the Creator through their traces and their substances, awaken the heedless, alert the ignorant, and confound the obstinate with their proof. For no one can deny His creation of them, and whoever created them is able to govern them in the aforementioned manner. And whoever is so is absolutely free from any partner, and whoever is so is able to do everything. Therefore He said: ﴿that Allah﴾, that is, the Sovereign Most High, to whom belongs all encompassing, ﴿is over all things﴾, that is, of other worlds, it is possible that they fall under His will, for it is in the sense of an object (maf'ul) of another world like this world, and more wondrous than it, and more wondrous than that wonder, without end, by deduction from this world. For whoever is able to bring a particle into existence from non-existence is able to bring into existence what is less than it, like it, and above it, without end, because there is no difference in that between a little and a lot, great or small. ﴿You will not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any disproportion﴾ [al-Mulk: 3]. And beware of turning to one who says that it is not possible for there to be anything more wondrous than this world. For that is a wicked philosophical doctrine, and the verse is a clear text refuting it, even if some of the heretics attribute it to al-Ghazali. I have no doubt that it was forged and attributed to him, for it is a wicked philosophical doctrine, as al-Ghazali's own testimony shows, as I explained in my book "Tahdim al-Arkan 'ala man qala laysa fi al-Imkan Abda' mimma Kana" (Demolishing the Pillars against One Who Said There Is Nothing in Possibility More Wondrous Than What Has Been), and my book "Dalalat al-Burhan 'ala anna fi al-Imkan Abda' mimma Kana" (The Indication of Proof That There Is in Possibility Something More Wondrous Than What Has Been), and my book "Itbaq al-Aghlal fi A'naq al-Dalal" (Locking the Shackles on the Necks of Misguidance). Although it is the doctrine of the philosophers, the most disbelieving apostate Ibn 'Arabi took it and deposited it in his Fusus and other of his books, and in some of them he relied upon al-Ghazali, perfecting his deception. May Allah protect us from his evil. Al-Ghazali is innocent of it by the testimony of what was found of his beliefs in the Ihya' and elsewhere. ﴿Competent﴾, that is, of perfect power.

Since the all-encompassing knowledge indicates complete power, and all names and attributes return to these two, He said: ﴿has encompassed﴾, for the completeness of His power, ﴿all things﴾, absolutely. And since He attributed the encompassing to Himself, Exalted is He, to glorify it, He specified its mode by a distinguishing accusative that is transferred from the agent, so He said: ﴿knowledge﴾. So to Him belongs complete expertise in what He commands of rulings, in knowing what is in their interests and corruptions. So treat Him as one who knows that His knowledge encompasses, and knows that He is watchful over you. So when you divorce, do what He commanded you, so that you may be safe in religion and blessed in the Hereafter and this world. And govern all your affairs in the same manner in which He governed your affairs in your nurture and your dwelling, His earth and His ceiling, for He placed in it all that you need, and spread out His bounty upon those who please Him and those who anger Him, and spread His forbearance and grace, and delayed His might and justice. He has removed from its last part its first, and between its summary and its detail. And Allah knows what is in the breasts.
